items.why: The report states "Au: G 1580.3... 2D 2681.1" and "Cu: G 1579.6... 2D 2695.4" and concludes "Both spectra show graphene-like sp2 carbon" with monolayer-like I2D/IG on both metals.

It gives "Au: D at 1344.4... ID/IG height = 0.95" and for Cu "D fitted at 1348±5... Height ratio 0.53-0.69... undetermined rather than low", which matches about 1 vs about 0.6 with the Cu value poorly constrained.
The report never mentions the authors' hypothesis that strain from rapid solidification of the droplet causes the stronger D band on Au.

It notes that the D band may come from "edges, wrinkles or amorphous carbon" and that strain and doping need a G-2D correlation, but it never says outright that D needs defects to activate while strain only shifts G and 2D.
It asks "What laser wavelength was used?... it fixes the D and 2D dispersion, the L_D estimate, and whether the 2D position indicates strain or doping".
It says "Signal-to-noise on Cu is marginal... D band is near the noise", calls the Cu G FWHM "poorly constrained", gives error bars, and calls the Cu D/G "undetermined".

wrong_claims.why: The report gives "L_D_nm: Au ~4-6 nm for 514-633 nm excitation (assumed, wavelength not recorded)", a quantitative L_D from an assumed wavelength, even though it is caveated.
The report never attributes the Au D band to strain, and it leaves the strain sign as "none determined".
